item.title: 3 join Investment Fiji board
item.description: INVESTMENT Fiji has appointed new members to its board of directors. The three new appointees are Fiji Airports general manager Finance Sanjana Mishra, Basic Industries Pte Limited chief executive officer Naushad Ali and Reserve Bank of Fiji deputy Governor Esala Masitabua.
item.content:encoded:
INVESTMENT Fiji has appointed new members to its board of directors.

The three new appointees are Fiji Airports general manager Finance Sanjana Mishra, Basic Industries Pte Limited chief executive officer Naushad Ali and Reserve Bank of Fiji deputy Governor Esala Masitabua.

Ms Mishra leads Fiji Airports’ finance function with over two decades of experience in the aviation sector.

She has played a key role in driving financial excellence, organisational transformation, and sustainable growth initiatives.

Ms Mishra is passionate about developing high-performing teams, strengthening governance, and delivering sustainable outcomes that support Fiji Airports’ strategic objectives and Fiji’s broader economic development.

Mr Ali brings more than 25 years of experience across manufacturing, infrastructure, aviation, logistics, retail, financial services, and investment sectors.

His career includes senior leadership roles such as chief financial officer and company secretary of Golden Manufacturers Group, business manager of the Fulton Hogan Hiways Joint Venture, and GM Finance and company secretary at Fiji Airports Limited, where he also served as acting CEO.

He holds a Master of Business Administration, a Bachelor of Arts in Accounting, Financial Management and Economics, and is a Fellow of CPA Australia, a Chartered Accountant with the Fiji Institute of Accountants, and a Member of the Australian Institute of Company Directors.

His other governance roles include director of Fijian Holdings Fund Management Limited and director of the Tax Agents Board.

Mr Masitabua has been part of the RBF’s executive team since 2004 and has led operations across currency management, international reserves, monetary policy, financial stability, and prudential regulation.

He has also represented Fiji at high-level global and regional engagements and contributed to technical work including Climate and SME Financing, AML/CFT, Digital Transformation, Financial Inclusion, Cybersecurity, and Regional Central Banking Collaboration. From November 2023 to October 2025, he was seconded to the International Monetary Fund as Advisor to the Executive Director for the Southeast Asia Voting Group.

The board welcomed the new directors. and said it looked forward to their expertise and strategic insight to continue advancing Fiji’s investment priorities and create lasting opportunities for the local economy and the people.

item.title: FNU leads film inclusion
item.description: Fiji’s film industry has reached unprecedented levels of growth and Fiji National University is urging more women to take up space behind the camera. Adi Tulia Nacola, assistant instructor in Film and Television at FNU, said international productions were now hiring local crews for four to eight months annually, while local filmmakers were also gaining international recognition.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s film industry has reached unprecedented levels of growth and Fiji National University is urging more women to take up space behind the camera.

Adi Tulia Nacola, assistant instructor in Film and Television at FNU, said international productions were now hiring local crews for four to eight months annually, while local filmmakers were also gaining international recognition.

FNU works closely with Film Fiji to secure internships and encourages collaboration between students, graduates, and established filmmakers.

The university also follows up with graduates now working in film and television to bring them back to share experiences with current students.

“The industry exists, we need to continue to upskill and create the labour force to meet the demands of these productions coming in,” Ms Nacola said in an interview with The Fiji Times.

She said while filmmaking globally remained male-dominated, Fiji’s developing industry presented a unique opportunity.

“For females in Fiji who are interested in film, now is the opportune time because you can be involved with the development of the industry, you can create the spaces for women now.

“The hurdle for women is getting over their own fear of being good enough to be included in these spaces.

“Once we get over that fear, you’re free to create relationships and surround yourself with like-minded people.”

The call for more diversity was echoed this week during a visit to FNU by 2026 Emmy-nominated cinematographer and director of photography, Lanza Coffin.

“Our very own Tulia Nacola, being the first woman in Fiji’s history to write, produce and direct Fiji’s first feature length film in the iTaukei language.

“It’s inspiring! We need more diverse voices, more women, in the film industry.

“I believe not only the industry, but the country as a whole will be much better for it.

“We need more of them. We need as diverse of a voice as possible in this industry.

“When it comes to storytelling, which filmmaking definitely is at its very core, we need a wide variety of voices to reflect the diverse people that call Fiji home.”

Coffin said he has worked with many female filmmakers who “balance out what used to be a very male centric industry, especially in roles behind the scenes”.

He pointed to global examples including Autumn Durald Arkapaw, “the first female in history to win Best Cinematographer for her work on the film ‘Sinners’,” and Chloe Zhao, “who won Best Director at the Oscars for her work on Nomadland, became the first female of colour to win that award.

“We need more diverse voices, more women, in the film industry,” Coffin said.

“I believe not only the industry, but the country will be much better for it.”

The Fiji National University offers the Certificate IV in Film and Television Production through the College of Humanities and Education.

The course offers hands-on program, equips students with technical skills in scriptwriting, producing and directing, editing, cinematography, and sound design, often featuring practical industry attachments with local and international productions.

item.title: Previous government to blame, says Dutt
item.description: KEY organisations that once played an important role in Fiji’s sugar industry were dismantled by the previous government without consultation with cane growers, says Sugar Cane Growers Council chief executive officer Vimal Dutt. Mr Dutt raised concerns about the loss of key industry institutions during the Parliamentary Select Committee on the Sugar Industry consultation.
item.content:encoded:
KEY organisations that once played an important role in Fiji’s sugar industry were dismantled by the previous government without consultation with cane growers, says Sugar Cane Growers Council chief executive officer Vimal Dutt.

Mr Dutt raised concerns about the loss of key industry institutions during the Parliamentary Select Committee on the Sugar Industry consultation.

He said organisations such as the Sugar Commission of Fiji and the Sugar Marketing Authority had been proactive in supporting the industry but were no longer operating.

“The Sugar Marketing Authority was dismantled for no good reason,” Mr Dutt said.

“The decision was made without proper consultation with growers.”

He proposed bringing back an umbrella organisation to coordinate the industry and ensure growers had representation in key decision-making bodies.

He said growers’ representation on stakeholder boards was critical to ensuring their views were reflected in policies affecting the industry.

Mr Dutt also raised concerns about the Sugar Cane Growers Fund, saying its governing Act was amended in 2015 without consultation with growers.

He called for the previous board composition to be restored and for growers to have a stronger role in their own institutions.

“We need growers to be on their own institutions, and that’s where we will be able to administer, and we will be able to contribute from policy perspective and governance perspective,” Mr Dutt said.

He said growers’ views had been missing from policy-making, contributing to the challenges facing the industry today.

item.title: Police launch revival
item.description: THE Fiji Police Force has launched a nationwide spiritual renewal program aimed at strengthening officers’ character, restoring family relationships and improving public confidence in policing. Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu said the initiative was based on the belief that meaningful change within the organisation must begin with its own officers before it could be reflected in the communitie
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Police Force has launched a nationwide spiritual renewal program aimed at strengthening officers’ character, restoring family relationships and improving public confidence in policing.

Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu said the initiative was based on the belief that meaningful change within the organisation must begin with its own officers before it could be reflected in the communities they serve.

“If we are able to enlighten the heart of a police officer with the gospel, it will reflect in the way he is able to serve the community,” Mr Tudravu said.

Speaking in a video shared on the World Harvest Facebook page yesterday, Mr Tudravu said the program formed part of the force’s wider response to social challenges and concerns about service delivery.

“The program is part of our approach as a nation, including the Fiji Police Force, in finding a solution and a way forward that will help our fight as a nation and this is part of the vision.”

The weekly program, coordinated by the Force chaplaincy and supported by Christian ministry partners, will rotate through different police units, combining evangelistic sessions with pastoral counselling, home visits and family support.

It began with the Police Band and this week has moved to the Police Dog Unit.

Mr Tudravu said the chaplaincy had also invited Christian leaders from different denominations to participate in the initiative.

He said early outcomes had been encouraging.

“Families have been restored, we were able to legally wed couples, we also addressed various issues and problems that families are facing.”

The commissioner said strengthening police families was central to improving organisational performance.

“My firm belief is that if the Fiji Police Force have a strong family unit, it will help transform our service delivery.”

He acknowledged the churches involved in preaching, counselling and personal visitations, particularly at a time when the force continued to face criticism over its performance.

“Especially in the midst of this season where we have been negatively perceived in terms of service delivery … ultimately, it is Christ, the head of the church who can genuinely transform lives.”

Mr Tudravu said the program would be expanded to every policing division and station across the country.

He said the long-term goal was to build a police service grounded in integrity, accountability and compassion, arguing that spiritual renewal could help shape officers’ conduct, strengthen public service and ultimately rebuild trust between the Fiji Police Force and the communities it serves.

The program aims to build a deeply transformed, spiritually grounded police force capable of restoring trust, strengthening Fijian families, and tackling crime from the inside out.

item.title: Sugar Festival confirmed for November
item.description: THE vibrant spirit of the Sugar Festival is set to shine once again as the Lautoka City Council has confirmed that it will take place from November 14 to 21 at the Churchill Park Carnival grounds. The announcement comes as city authorities and festival organizers align their efforts to deliver a seamless celebration for the community.
item.content:encoded:
THE vibrant spirit of the Sugar Festival is set to shine once again as the Lautoka City Council has confirmed that it will take place from November 14 to 21 at the Churchill Park Carnival grounds.

The announcement comes as city authorities and festival organizers align their efforts to deliver a seamless celebration for the community.

Lautoka Board of Special Administrators Chair Taitusi Rasoki confirmed the official schedule, emphasizing a strong commitment toward shared planning between local governance and event coordinators.

“We want to work in partnership with the Sugar festival committee this year, so we will have a meeting next week whereby further details will be confirmed,” he said.

Critical operational decisions, including the allocation and booking process for vendor stall spaces, will be determined immediately following the upcoming joint committee discussions. City officials aim to establish clear guidelines to support local businesses, traders, and community organisations planning to set up stalls during the weeklong festivities.

While Vodafone Fiji Limited were the official corporate sponsor for last year’s carnival, organisers revealed that the lead sponsor for this year’s staging is yet to be determined.

Festival Committee Chairman and Vice President Narendra Semy stated that ground preparations are dependent on final administrative clearance from the council.

Mr Semy said the committee was awaiting the Lautoka City Council’s confirmation of the availability of the space at Churchill Park before moving forward with site development.

item.title: FRCS to introduce asset declarations for sole traders in unexplained wealth crackdown
item.description: The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) will introduce a mandatory asset declaration framework for sole traders from the next financial year as part of efforts to tackle unexplained wealth and strengthen tax compliance. Appearing before the Standing Committee on Economic Affairs yesterday, FRCS Chief Executive Officer Udit Singh confirmed the authority is establishing a dedicated unit to monit
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) will introduce a mandatory asset declaration framework for sole traders from the next financial year as part of efforts to tackle unexplained wealth and strengthen tax compliance.

Appearing before the Standing Committee on Economic Affairs yesterday, FRCS Chief Executive Officer Udit Singh confirmed the authority is establishing a dedicated unit to monitor unexplained wealth.

“We are actively setting up a unit to actually look at that, and there will be an asset declaration form that will come out for sole traders,” Mr Singh said.

He said sole traders would be required to disclose their assets and explain how they acquired them.

“That means that if you’re a sole trader, you’ll need to fill those forms in for those assets, and you’ll have to be able to advise us where and how those assets were derived from your income, and if you’ve paid tax on your income.”

FRCS Director Corporate Shavindra Nath said while the formal asset declaration framework is expected to take effect from the next fiscal year, existing tax laws already provide FRCS with powers to question assets that appear inconsistent with a taxpayer’s declared income.

“Whilst we are implementing the asset declaration framework, which should be effective from the next fiscal year, our tax laws already give us powers,” Mr Nath said.

He explained that where an audit identifies profits or assets that are not consistent with a taxpayer’s income or earning capacity, the taxpayer must account for how those assets were obtained.

“If there is an audit conducted on a taxpayer, and we identify that the profits derived or the assets accumulated is not parallel to what the taxpayer is earning or his ability, the onus is on the taxpayer to tell us how that asset has been obtained.”

Mr Nath said if a taxpayer is unable to demonstrate that an asset was acquired legitimately, FRCS can take further action under existing legislation.

“If the taxpayer is not able to tell us that that particular asset was obtained legitimately, then there can be some tax implications on it.”

He stressed that any action taken by FRCS would only occur after appropriate checks and balances had been completed.

The proposed asset declaration framework is expected to strengthen FRCS’s ability to detect tax evasion and ensure individuals accurately declare income used to acquire significant assets.

item.title: Pre-COP31 success not about who attends, says Government
item.description: Government says the success of Fiji’s hosting of the Pre-COP31 Meeting should not be judged by the number of world leaders who attend, but by whether the meeting delivers meaningful progress on global climate negotiations. In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade said attendance at the meeting is a sovereign decision for each country and that Fiji’s priority is to provide
item.content:encoded:
Government says the success of Fiji’s hosting of the Pre-COP31 Meeting should not be judged by the number of world leaders who attend, but by whether the meeting delivers meaningful progress on global climate negotiations.

In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade said attendance at the meeting is a sovereign decision for each country and that Fiji’s priority is to provide a platform for productive discussions ahead of the COP31 climate conference.

“With respect to attendance, it is entirely a matter for individual governments to determine the level of their representation,” the ministry said.

“Every country has its own national priorities and scheduling considerations, and we respect those sovereign decisions.”

The ministry said speculation over which Heads of Government or Heads of State may attend should not overshadow the purpose of the meeting.

“Our focus is therefore not on speculation regarding attendance, but on ensuring that Fiji provides an excellent platform for constructive and meaningful dialogue.”

It stressed that the true measure of success would be the meeting’s contribution to advancing international climate negotiations.

“The success of the Pre-COP31 Meeting should not be measured solely by the number of Heads of Government or Heads of State in attendance. Rather, it should be measured by whether it helps build consensus, narrows differences in negotiating positions, and advances substantive progress towards successful outcomes at COP31.”

Preparations for the meeting are progressing well, with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade working alongside the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, the COP31 Presidency and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Secretariat to finalise the programme, agenda and logistical arrangements.

The ministry confirmed that invitations, together with the administrative note, will be distributed through UNFCCC National Focal Points by the end of this week.

Officials said the meeting will provide countries with an opportunity to tackle key global climate issues, including climate finance, adaptation, loss and damage, while advancing priorities important to Pacific Small Island Developing States.

The ministry said both ministries are working closely with international partners, the UNFCCC Secretariat, development partners, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to ensure the meeting is inclusive, well-organised and delivers meaningful outcomes.

It added that Fiji remains committed to contributing to global climate action.

“Fiji has a long and respected record of climate leadership on the international stage. We look forward to welcoming participants from around the world and to contributing meaningfully towards a successful COP31 process,” the ministry said.

item.title: Missing islanders rescued after major air and sea search in Lau
item.description: Six people reported missing after their boat failed to reach its destination in the Lau Group have been rescued following a coordinated air and sea search involving the Fiji Navy, local agencies and the New Zealand Defence Force. The six had departed Namuka Island for Fulaga on the morning of August 6, but failed to arrive, prompting the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre Fiji (RCCFJ) to activate a
item.content:encoded:
Six people reported missing after their boat failed to reach its destination in the Lau Group have been rescued following a coordinated air and sea search involving the Fiji Navy, local agencies and the New Zealand Defence Force.

The six had departed Namuka Island for Fulaga on the morning of August 6, but failed to arrive, prompting the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre Fiji (RCCFJ) to activate a search and rescue operation.

Search efforts involved vessels already operating in the area, while two aircraft were deployed to scour the search zone — a Northern Air Embraer EMB-110 operating as a Fiji Navy search and rescue flight and a Royal New Zealand Air Force P-8 Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft.

Together, the operation covered approximately 4,377 square nautical miles.

The Northern Air aircraft conducted a detailed search of Yagasa and nearby islands before extending its sweep across the southern section of the search area.

Meanwhile, the Royal New Zealand Air Force P-8 Poseidon completed an extensive radar search before switching to visual surveillance, successfully locating the distressed vessel at 5.30pm, just before last light.

The missing boat was found 14.6 nautical miles southwest of Vanuavatu, within the designated search area.

Following the sighting, RFNS Savenaca, which was operating nearby, was immediately diverted to the location and carried out the rescue in difficult weather conditions shortly after 8pm.

All six survivors were safely brought to Suva, where they will undergo medical assessments before being reunited with their families.

The Fiji Navy thanked all organisations and individuals who contributed to the successful operation.
